abstract: Microsoft's 2024 Work Trend Index report finds that 75% of global knowledge workers now use generative AI at work, with adoption nearly doubling in six months. While AI adoption is accelerating and workers report significant productivity gains, organizational leaders struggle with strategic implementation, with 60% lacking a clear plan. The report identifies a paradox where workers fear job displacement while employers face talent shortages, and reveals that AI aptitude is becoming as important as experience in hiring decisions.
keyFindings: 75% of global knowledge workers use AI tools at work, with 46% having started within the last six months; adoption in enterprises with 500+ employees reached 60%, up from 40% a year prior.
78% of AI users are bringing their own AI tools to work without organizational authorization (BYOAI), driven by work overload—68% report struggling with pace and volume, and 46% feel burned out.
71% of leaders say they would hire a less experienced candidate with AI skills over a more experienced candidate without them, and 66% say they would not hire someone lacking AI skills.

AI power users (those using AI multiple times weekly) save more than 30 minutes per day and report 92% say AI makes overwhelming workload manageable, 92% boost creativity, and 91% feel more motivated.

Projected skill changes are expected to accelerate from 50% by 2030 to 68% due to generative AI; 68% of fastest-growing US job roles did not exist 20 years ago, with 12% of recruiters already creating new roles tied to generative AI use.
methodology: Multi-method research combining: (1) Work Trend Index survey of 31,000 full-time knowledge workers across 31 countries conducted February 15-March 28, 2024 by Edelman Data & Intelligence; (2) LinkedIn Economic Graph data analyzing 1 billion+ members and labor market trends; (3) analysis of trillions of Microsoft 365 productivity signals from commercial customers in rolling 28-day periods; (4) six-month randomized controlled trial of 60 Copilot customers (3,000 individuals) observing natural work environment usage; (5) LinkedIn Executive Confidence Index survey of ~5,000 VP+ level members (March 4-19, 2024); (6) LinkedIn Workplace Learning Report of 1,636 L&D/HR professionals and 1,063 learners; (7) 2024 Global Marketing Jobs Outlook of 1,577 senior B2B marketing leaders.
qualifiers: Results weighted and aggregated globally across 31 markets; US results include additional 2,800-person regional sample. Copilot study results are preliminary. LinkedIn Executive Confidence Index and Workplace Learning Report data are unpublished/internal sources. Some data excludes EU usage and education segments. Copilot meeting summarization data represents only intentional queries, not Teams Intelligent Recap activity. Labor market projections based on linear extrapolation with generative AI impact scenarios. Results represent LinkedIn platform membership lens; variances between platform membership and overall market population not accounted for. Report acknowledges uncertainty: 59% of leaders worry about quantifying AI productivity gains, and 60% of leaders worry their organization lacks a plan and vision for AI implementation.
